title: Jira vs Plane
comparison_markdown:
# Jira vs Plane (2026)

## Overview
Jira and Plane are two project management tools designed to help teams organize and track their work. This comparison is beneficial for teams currently using Jira and considering switching to Plane, likely due to Plane's self-hosted option and free cost. The core use case for both tools is issue tracking and project management, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Jira charges a per-user monthly fee, while Plane is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: Plane allows teams to host their own data, while Jira stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Jira has a more straightforward setup process, while Plane requires more technical expertise to self-host.
* Scalability: Jira is designed to handle large teams and enterprises, while Plane is better suited for smaller teams and organizations.
* Integration with Git: Jira has native integration with Git, while Plane requires a third-party plugin to achieve similar functionality.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Jira | Plane |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $7.75-$14.50/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $387.50-$725/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,550-$2,900/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Jira
* Pros:
  + Easy to set up and use
  + Native integration with Git
  + Scalable for large teams and enterprises
  + Wide range of third-party integrations available
  + Strong customer support
* Cons:
  + Expensive, especially for large teams
  + Limited control over data storage and security
  + Proprietary license
### Plane
* Pros:
  + Free and self-hosted
  + High degree of control over data storage and security
  + Customizable and extensible
  + Apache 2.0 license
  + Cost-effective for small to medium-sized teams
* Cons:
  + Requires technical expertise to set up and maintain
  + Limited native integrations with other tools
  + May not be suitable for very large teams or enterprises
  + Limited customer support

## When to Choose Each
Jira is a good choice for large teams and enterprises that need a scalable and easy-to-use project management tool, and are willing to pay a premium for it. Plane, on the other hand, is a good choice for small to medium-sized teams that want a high degree of control over their data and are comfortable with self-hosting and maintaining their own software.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Jira data in CSV or JSON format.
2. Set up a Plane instance on your own server.
3. Use the Plane import tool to import your Jira data.
4. Configure any necessary plugins or integrations in Plane.
5. Test your Plane instance to ensure everything is working as expected.

## Our Take
Plane is not yet production-ready for most users, as it still lacks some of the polish and features of Jira. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Plane's API is still in development, which may limit its integrations with other tools. However, for small to medium-sized teams that value control over their data and are comfortable with self-hosting, Plane is a clear winner, and we recommend switching from Jira to take advantage of its cost-effectiveness and customizability.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) that don't need native Git integration
* Medium-sized teams (10-50 users) that want more control over their data
* Teams that are currently using Jira's free plan and are outgrowing it
* Teams that are comfortable with self-hosting and maintaining their own software
* Teams that prioritize cost-effectiveness and customizability over ease of use

## FAQ
### Can I use Plane for free?
Yes, Plane is free and self-hosted, which means you can use it at no cost beyond the cost of hosting your own server.
### Is Plane as scalable as Jira?
No, Plane is not yet as scalable as Jira, and may not be suitable for very large teams or enterprises.
### Can I integrate Plane with other tools?
Yes, Plane has a growing ecosystem of plugins and integrations, but it may not have the same level of native integration as Jira.
### How do I migrate my data from Jira to Plane?
You can export your Jira data in CSV or JSON format and then use the Plane import tool to import it.
### Is Plane's API fully developed?
Not yet, Plane's API is still in development, which may limit its integrations with other tools.

title: Trello vs WeKan
comparison_markdown:
# Trello vs WeKan (2026)

## Overview
Trello and WeKan are project management tools designed to help teams organize and manage their tasks and workflows. This comparison is beneficial for teams currently using Trello who are considering switching to WeKan, possibly due to the desire for more control over their data or the need for a self-hosted solution. The core use case for both tools is team collaboration and task management, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more autonomy over their data and workflow.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Trello offers a free plan with limited features, while WeKan is completely free as it is self-hosted.
* Data Ownership: WeKan allows teams to have full ownership and control over their data, whereas Trello stores data on its servers.
* Setup Complexity: WeKan requires more technical expertise to set up and maintain, especially for self-hosting, compared to Trello's straightforward sign-up process.
* Scalability: Trello is designed to scale with large teams and enterprises, while WeKan's scalability depends on the server capabilities of the self-hosted environment.
* Integration Difference: Trello has a wider range of integrations with third-party services, including Google Drive and Slack, whereas WeKan's integrations are more limited but can be extended through its open-source nature.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Trello | WeKan |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $5+/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $250/month (standard plan) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1000/month (standard plan) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Trello
* Easy to use and set up
* Wide range of integrations with third-party services
* Scalable for large teams and enterprises
* Mobile apps for on-the-go access
* Limited control over data for free plan users
### WeKan
* Completely free and open-source
* Self-hosting option for full data control
* Customizable through its open-source nature
* Limited integrations with third-party services
* Requires technical expertise for setup and maintenance

## When to Choose Each
Trello is the better choice for teams that prioritize ease of use, wide integration capabilities, and scalability without worrying about the costs associated with each user. It's ideal for large teams or enterprises that need a straightforward, cloud-based project management solution. On the other hand, WeKan is suited for teams or individuals who value data privacy, customization, and the freedom to host their solution on their own servers. This makes it a good fit for small to medium-sized teams, especially those with the technical expertise to handle self-hosting and customization.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Trello boards in JSON format using Trello's built-in export feature.
2. Set up your WeKan server, either locally or on a cloud platform, by following WeKan's installation guide.
3. Use WeKan's import tool to migrate your Trello data, ensuring that your boards, lists, and cards are properly transferred.
4. Configure any necessary integrations or customizations in WeKan to match your previous Trello setup.
5. Test your WeKan installation to ensure all data and functionality have been successfully migrated.

## Our Take
WeKan is not yet production-ready for most users due to its requirement for technical expertise in setup and maintenance. While it offers a high degree of customization and control over data, this comes at the cost of ease of use and widespread adoption. A specific technical limitation worth noting is WeKan's lack of native mobile apps, which can limit its accessibility for teams that rely heavily on mobile devices for their workflow. For teams prioritizing data ownership and customization over ease of use and scalability, WeKan is a viable alternative to Trello, but for most users, Trello remains the more accessible and user-friendly option.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) who prioritize data control and do not need extensive integrations.
* Technical teams that can handle self-hosting and customization.
* Individuals or teams who do not need mobile apps for their workflow.
* Teams currently using Trello's free plan and looking to avoid per-user costs.
* Organizations with strict data privacy requirements that necessitate self-hosting.

## FAQ
### Can I use WeKan without self-hosting?
WeKan is designed to be self-hosted, but there are cloud hosting options available that can simplify the setup process. However, these may still require some technical knowledge.
### Is WeKan as easy to use as Trello?
No, WeKan requires more technical expertise to set up and customize compared to Trello's straightforward interface.
### Can I migrate my Trello data to WeKan?
Yes, you can export your Trello data in JSON format and import it into WeKan using its import tool.
### Does WeKan have mobile apps?
Not yet, WeKan does not have native mobile apps, which can be a limitation for teams relying on mobile access.
### Is WeKan completely free?
Yes, WeKan is completely free and open-source, with no per-user costs, but you will need to consider the cost of hosting your own server.

title: Dropbox vs Nextcloud
comparison_markdown:
# Dropbox vs Nextcloud

## Overview

Dropbox is one of the original cloud storage services offering simple file sync. Nextcloud is the most popular self-hosted cloud platform combining file storage, calendar, contacts, video calls, and 400+ apps.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Dropbox charges $9.99-$16.58/user/month; Nextcloud is free to self-host
- **Storage**: Nextcloud storage is limited only by your server disk space
- **Feature breadth**: Nextcloud is far more than storage; it is a full Google Workspace alternative
- **Privacy**: Nextcloud on your own server means only you can access your data
- **Setup**: Dropbox is instant; Nextcloud requires Docker setup

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Dropbox | Nextcloud |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | $9.99-$16.58/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | ~$500/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | ~$1,998/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Dropbox

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Nextcloud

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [nextcloud/server](https://github.com/nextcloud/server) * ~27k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Dropbox if:** Dropbox suits individuals or small teams wanting simple reliable file sync with no infrastructure to manage.

**Choose Nextcloud if:** Nextcloud suits privacy-focused organizations wanting to eliminate cloud subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Download all Dropbox files locally, then upload to Nextcloud via the web interface or desktop sync client.

## Our Take

Nextcloud is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Dropbox tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Nextcloud instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Dropbox, switching to self-hosted Nextcloud will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Dropbox until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Dropbox paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Nextcloud free to use?
Yes. Nextcloud is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Dropbox to Nextcloud?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Dropbox data, follow the Nextcloud import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Nextcloud get regular updates?
Yes. Nextcloud has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Nextcloud without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Nextcloud development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced July 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Dropbox](https://dropbox.com) and [Nextcloud](https://nextcloud.com) before making decisions.*
meta_description: Nextcloud is a free, self-hosted alternative to Dropbox. Compare pricing, features, and migration steps. See full comparison.

title: Microsoft Teams vs Mattermost
comparison_markdown:
# Microsoft Teams vs Mattermost (2026)

## Overview
Microsoft Teams and Mattermost are two popular communication and collaboration platforms designed for teams and organizations. They offer a range of features, including messaging, video conferencing, and file sharing, making them ideal for remote teams, businesses, and enterprises. The core use case for both tools is to facilitate teamwork and communication, and someone might consider switching from Microsoft Teams to Mattermost for better data ownership and control.

## Key Differences
* **Cost**: Microsoft Teams offers a free version, as well as paid plans starting at $6 per user per month, while Mattermost is free and open-source, with optional self-hosting.
* **Data Ownership**: Mattermost allows users to self-host their data, giving them full control and ownership, whereas Microsoft Teams stores data on Microsoft's servers.
* **Setup Complexity**: Microsoft Teams is generally easier to set up, with a more streamlined onboarding process, while Mattermost requires more technical expertise to self-host.
* **Scalability**: Microsoft Teams is designed to scale with large enterprises, while Mattermost is also scalable, but may require more configuration and optimization.
* **Integration Difference**: Microsoft Teams has native integration with Microsoft Office 365, while Mattermost has integration with a wide range of third-party tools and services through its open API.

## Pricing Comparison

Mattermost, on the other hand, is suitable for teams and organizations that value data ownership and control, and are willing to self-host their own servers. It's also a good choice for teams that require a high degree of customization and flexibility.

## Migration Path

3. Import your exported data into Mattermost using the Mattermost API or a third-party tool.
4. Configure any necessary integrations with third-party tools and services.

We recommend switching to Mattermost if you're a small to medium-sized team that requires a high degree of customization and flexibility, and doesn't need native integration with Microsoft Office 365.

* Organizations that require a high degree of scalability and flexibility

# Google Workspace vs Nextcloud

## Overview

Google suite of cloud productivity tools including Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Meet, and Calendar. is a popular proprietary tool in the productivity space. Nextcloud is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Google Workspace costs $6-$18/user/month; Nextcloud is Free (self-hosted)
- **License**: Google Workspace is Proprietary; Nextcloud is AGPL 3.0
- **Data ownership**: Nextcloud can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Nextcloud eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Nextcloud has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Google Workspace | Nextcloud |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | $6-$18/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | ~$300/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | ~$1,200/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Google Workspace

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Nextcloud

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [nextcloud/server](https://github.com/nextcloud/server) * ~27k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Google Workspace if:** Google Workspace is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Nextcloud if:** Nextcloud is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from Google Workspace in its standard export format, review Nextcloud import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Nextcloud is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Google Workspace tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Nextcloud instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Google Workspace, switching to self-hosted Nextcloud will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Google Workspace until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Google Workspace paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Nextcloud free to use?
Yes. Nextcloud is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Google Workspace to Nextcloud?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Google Workspace data, follow the Nextcloud import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Nextcloud get regular updates?
Yes. Nextcloud has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Nextcloud without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Nextcloud development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced July 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Google Workspace](https://workspace.google.com) and [Nextcloud](https://nextcloud.com) before making decisions.*
